_note: The first career's tutorial. Percy talks the player through one course, start to first close of play. Each step is done when its doneWhen holds; steps already done are skipped. doneWhen is a condition the engine checks (ownsCourse, firstHoleHasTee, firstHoleHasGreen, firstHolePlayable, courseReady, courseOpen, dayPassed, facilityBought) or event:<name> for something only the screen knows (the app calls TutorialState.record). screen and anchor tell the app where to point.

steps.title: Percy Hollis, at your service
lines: Good morning. Percy Hollis. I've been secretary at more golf clubs than I care to remember, and I've been asked to keep an eye on you.
You have two hundred thousand pounds and no golf course. Let's see about fixing the second part before you spend the first.

steps.title: Land for sale
lines: This is Britain, or the golfing parts of it. The pins are land for sale.
Cheap up north, eye watering down south. A quiet sale you can simply buy. Sealed bids mean one offer, opened on the closing day, and may the best chequebook win.

steps.title: Buy your first plot
lines: Start small. A cheap nine holer in the north is no disgrace; half the great clubs began as a farmer's field and a man with a mower.
Tap a quiet sale and buy it outright.

steps.title: Every hole starts with a tee
lines: Bare land. Lovely. Now, golfers are simple creatures: they need somewhere to start and somewhere to finish.
Pick the tee tool and tap near the bottom of the hole.

steps.title: And a green to finish
lines: Now a green, up towards the top. Paint a decent sized one; nobody enjoys putting on a postage stamp.
Then drop the pin on it with the pin tool.

steps.title: Fairway, bunkers, the fun bit
lines: Technically that's a golf hole. Practically, it's a field. Paint a fairway from tee to green, and a bunker or two where a careless drive might land.
The card below the hole marks it out of ten. Golfers like variety, a bit of danger and a fair chance. They don't like the same hole three times running.

steps.title: The other holes
lines: Every hole needs a tee and a green before we can open. Swipe across to move between them.
If you're in a hurry, Auto layout will rough one out for you. It costs the same as building it by hand, and it shows.

steps.title: Open for business
lines: There. A golf course. I've seen worse. I've played worse, mostly in Kent.
Set a green fee on the Run tab and open the gates. Too dear and they'll walk away; too cheap and you'll go bust being popular.

steps.title: Watch a round
lines: Golfers will turn up through the day. Do watch one; it's the best way to see what your holes are really like.
I shall be commentating, whether you like it or not.

steps.title: Close of play
lines: The day runs from seven till seven. Speed the clock up if you're impatient; I'm told it's a modern affliction.
At close of play you'll get the books: who came, what they paid, and what it cost to keep the grass alive.

steps.title: What they said
lines: Every golfer leaves a review. Read them. They are rude, unfair and occasionally right.
Good reviews build your reputation a little each day. Reputation brings bigger crowds, higher fees and, in time, proper tournaments.

steps.title: A roof over their heads
lines: Your reputation can only climb so high without a clubhouse. Golfers will forgive a lot, but not the lack of a bar.
Build one on the Club tab when the money allows.

steps.title: Over to you
lines: That's the lot. From here it's land, holes, golfers and money, in roughly that order of difficulty.
The ultimate prize is The Championship. You'll need a great links course and a reputation to match. No pressure. I'll be in the bar.
